enumDescriptions.SKU: Product SKU identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.GTIN: Global Trade Item Number for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OFFERING_ID: AdCP offering identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.JOB_ID: Job posting identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.HOTEL_ID: Hotel property identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.FLIGHT_ID: Flight route identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.VEHICLE_ID: Vehicle listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.LISTING_ID: Real estate listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.STORE_ID: Store location identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.PROGRAM_ID: Education program identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.DESTINATION_ID: Travel destination identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.CREATIVE_VARIANT_ID: Seller-assigned creative variant identifier, passed through at serve time
enumDescriptions.APP_ITEM_ID: Mobile app identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.ITEM_NAME: Name/title of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: name). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_DESCRIPTION: Description of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: description). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_TAGLINE: Short promotional tagline of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: tagline). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE: Price amount of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.amount). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE_CURRENCY: ISO 4217 currency code of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.currency). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.

external:enums/macro-resolver.json.title: Macro Processing Actor
external:enums/macro-resolver.json.description: Protocol role authorized to translate the token or bind its concrete value.

enumDescriptions.buyer: The buyer agent acts before submission.
enumDescriptions.creative_agent: The creative agent executing build_creative, preview_creative, or validate_input performs the declared build-time operation.
enumDescriptions.seller: The AdCP seller or its execution adapter acts during trafficking or serving.
enumDescriptions.request_executor: The component executing the governed request acts, whether a client player, publisher player, SSAI service, or another request executor.
enumDescriptions.source_ad_server: The originating creative/ad server acts on its own native token.

external:enums/macro-value-context.json.title: Macro Value Context
external:enums/macro-value-context.json.description: Syntactic occurrence context supported by the first macro contract. Substitution inside arbitrary JavaScript, JSON, or HTML text is intentionally not inferred; use `opaque` and preserve it unless a later governed context is added.

external:core/macro-encoding.json.title: Macro Encoding
external:core/macro-encoding.json.description: Exact encoding profile applied to a concrete substitution value. `rfc3986` encodes UTF-8 bytes outside the RFC 3986 unreserved set once per depth. `iab_vast_uri` follows the cited IAB VAST macro registry, including its array serialization rules, and is exactly one pass.

external:core/macro-translation-target.j.title: Macro Translation Target
external:core/macro-translation-target.j.description: The exact downstream-native token produced by a `translate_to_native` operation. The output asset replaces the source declaration with a declaration for this token and its next operation.

external:enums/macro-mapping-status.json.title: Macro Mapping Status
external:enums/macro-mapping-status.json.description: Evidence level connecting a dialect-local macro meaning to the AdCP universal vocabulary.

enumDescriptions.verified_universal: The cited dialect mapping verifies an AdCP universal semantic.
enumDescriptions.dialect_defined: The dialect defines the token, but no AdCP universal semantic is asserted.
enumDescriptions.unresolved: No safe meaning is established; the token remains byte-preserved.

external:core/geo-region-support.json.title: Geographic Region Support
external:core/geo-region-support.json.description: Country- and value-aware support for selecting canonical ISO 3166-2 subdivisions. all_values is exhaustive for the values active in the seller's support snapshot when the declaration is issued; it does not automatically include values introduced by a later catalog revision. values is an exact finite subset. In seller-wide capabilities, each declared value is individually supported within the response scope, but the declaration does not promise that values are jointly composable or available through the same execution route or account. In Product.overlay_support, the declared values form the binding set of executable targeting permissions for that Product, subject to its declared limits; support does not itself guarantee inventory for every selection.

countries.description: Selectable ISO subdivision values keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country.

all_values.description: Every protocol-valid ISO 3166-2 subdivision active in this declaration's support snapshot is selectable. Values introduced by a later catalog revision are not included automatically.

values.description: Exact finite selectable subset of ISO 3166-2 identifiers for this country.

catalog_version.description: Optional opaque ISO subdivision catalog or seller-mapping version that identifies the support snapshot. It is provenance, not part of subdivision identity.

as_of.description: Optional date on which the seller last validated this support declaration.

max_values_per_package.description: Optional maximum number of region values selectable on one package.

max_packages.description: Optional maximum number of independently region-targeted packages created from this configured product.

external:core/postal-area-support.json.title: Postal Area Support
external:core/postal-area-support.json.description: Declares supported postal area systems. Native support is keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country with arrays of country-local postal systems. Deprecated country-fused boolean aliases may be included during migration.

external:enums/legacy-postal-system.json.title: Country-Fused Postal Code System
external:enums/legacy-postal-system.json.description: Deprecated country-fused postal code systems for geographic targeting. Prefer postal-system with an explicit ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country on postal area objects.

external:core/geo-place-system.json.title: Geographic Place Identifier System
external:core/geo-place-system.json.description: Collision-safe identifier namespace for geographic places. Registered tokens have protocol-defined semantics. Unregistered systems MUST use an absolute HTTPS URI controlled by the catalog owner; consumers compare URI systems as exact opaque strings.

external:core/geo-place-support.json.title: Geographic Place System Support
external:core/geo-place-support.json.description: Declares exact country-to-place-type support plus catalog resolution and version metadata for one place identifier system. The country map avoids falsely implying a Cartesian product of countries and types.

countries.description: Supported place types keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country. Only explicitly listed country/type pairs are supported.

external:core/geo-place-type.json.title: Geographic Place Type
external:core/geo-place-type.json.description: Canonical place classification. Registered tokens have protocol-defined meanings. Catalog-specific classifications without a registered mapping MUST use an absolute HTTPS URI controlled by the vocabulary owner; consumers compare URI types as exact opaque strings.

external:core/geo-place-catalog-capabili.title: Geographic Place Catalog Capability
external:core/geo-place-catalog-capabili.description: Catalog version and resolution contract for one supported place identifier system. Versions are exact opaque strings, not ordered ranges.

source.description: Optional catalog dataset or derivative-source identifier. This records provenance/coverage and does not change the identifier namespace in system.

current_version.description: Version applied when a buyer omits system_version. Sellers MUST echo this version on persisted package state.

supported_versions.description: Exact catalog versions accepted for new targeting or target-changing updates. Must include current_version. Removing a version does not mutate or silently invalidate targets already pinned to it.

x-adcp-validation.description: JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express scalar membership in a sibling array; conformance tooling MUST verify current_version is present in supported_versions.

external:core/geo-place-resolver.json.title: Geographic Place Resolver
external:core/geo-place-resolver.json.description: Machine-readable HTTP resolver for converting unresolved place names into seller-accepted stable identifiers or refreshing an existing identifier. Clients send an HTTPS GET to url using the query parameters in get-geo-place-resolution-request.json and validate a 200 application/json response against get-geo-place-resolution-response.json. Non-200 responses are errors, not empty results. Clients MUST apply SSRF protections. seller_credentials may be used only when url has the same origin as the seller's AdCP endpoint.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint accepting the standard geo-place resolution query parameters.

auth.description: Authentication mode. seller_credentials means use the same authorization credentials as the seller's AdCP endpoint and is valid only for a same-origin resolver URL; credentials MUST NOT be forwarded cross-origin.

external:enums/age-verification-method.j.title: Age Verification Method
external:enums/age-verification-method.j.description: Methods for verifying user age for compliance. Does not include 'inferred' as it is not accepted for regulatory compliance.

external:core/locale-tag.json.title: Language Tag
external:core/locale-tag.json.description: A well-formed BCP 47 language tag used by AdCP only as language identity. Script and region may refine that identity; other valid BCP 47 subtags remain part of tag matching but do not make this a general locale-settings object. It does not determine currency, time zone, number/date formatting, market, or legal jurisdiction. The AdCP canonical wire profile requires lower-case language and variants, title-case script, and upper-case region (for example `en-US`, `zh-Hant-TW`, or `x-private`). RFC 5646 comparisons are case-insensitive and its case regularization is optional; AdCP intentionally requires this stricter single wire spelling and receivers MUST reject differently cased tags rather than silently normalizing them. The schema pattern enforces the AdCP casing profile and extension structure for commonly used tags; conforming receivers additionally validate the complete RFC 5646 grammar and registry rules. Every new AdCP field carrying BCP 47 language identity or a concrete language range MUST reference this schema instead of declaring independent string constraints.

external:enums/match-type.json.title: Match Type
external:enums/match-type.json.description: Keyword targeting match type. broad: ads may serve on queries semantically related to the keyword. phrase: ads serve when the query contains the keyword phrase. exact: ads serve only when the query matches the keyword exactly.

enumDescriptions.broad: Ads may serve on queries semantically related to the keyword
enumDescriptions.phrase: Ads serve when the query contains the keyword phrase in order
enumDescriptions.exact: Ads serve only when the query matches the keyword exactly

external:enums/transport-mode.json.title: Transport Mode
external:enums/transport-mode.json.description: Transportation modes for isochrone-based catchment area calculations. Determines how travel time translates to geographic reach.

enumDescriptions.walking: Pedestrian travel on walkable paths and sidewalks
enumDescriptions.cycling: Bicycle travel on roads and cycle paths
enumDescriptions.driving: Motor vehicle travel on road networks
enumDescriptions.public_transport: Public transit including bus, rail, metro, and ferry

external:enums/uid-type.json.title: UID Type
external:enums/uid-type.json.description: Type of user identifier. Used in audience sync, event logging, and TMP identity match requests to tell the receiver how to interpret and resolve the identifier; some types, including PAIR, are publisher-scoped rather than universal identity-graph tokens.

enumDescriptions.rampid: LiveRamp RampID maintained form (XY, 32 bytes on the wire)
enumDescriptions.rampid_derived: LiveRamp RampID derived form (Xi, 48 bytes on the wire)
enumDescriptions.pairid: Publisher Addressable Identity via IAB Tech Lab PAIR. The OpenRTB profile uses User.eids[].source pair-protocol.com, EID.mm 3, EID.matcher set to the publisher's canonical ads.txt ownerdomain, and uids[].atype 3. The URL-safe Base64-encoded KsKp Publisher Identifier must be interpreted with that matcher scope. It is stable across a publisher's advertiser matches only within a Ks key epoch; Ks rotates every 30 days, and current and prior Publisher Identifiers can overlap during rollover. TMP identity objects do not carry matcher or ownerdomain, so a bridge requires an authenticated out-of-band binding to preserve PAIR scope.
enumDescriptions.hashed_email: SHA-256 hashed email address. Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — unsalted SHA-256 of the email namespace is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries; treat as PII. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.
enumDescriptions.publisher_first_party: Publisher's own first-party identifier, opaque to buyers
enumDescriptions.world_id_nullifier: World ID nullifier — a Sybil-resistant, relying-party-scoped, unlinkable pseudonym. Carries NO personhood or age assertion on its own; trust comes only from an accompanying verified `attestation`, never from this type tag. Distinct from the `world_id` value in the age-verification-method enum, which names a method, not an identifier.
enumDescriptions.other: Other universal ID type (specify in ext)

external:core/audience-activation-method.title: Audience Activation Method
external:core/audience-activation-method.description: One way buyer audience data can reach a seller for targeting. The pattern field discriminates the entry; each pattern carries only its own fields. Two patterns are AdCP-canonical (sync_audiences, tmp_identity_match); the rest describe integration paths that move data outside the protocol while remaining discoverable through it. Vendor identity is a BrandRef domain so new platforms declare a domain rather than waiting on an enum change. Experimental (x-status: experimental): the audience-activation surface — this schema, product.audience_activation, audience_targeting.supported_activation_methods, and the audience_activation_methods product filter — is new and not yet field-tested across parties. Sellers that implement it MUST list media_buy.audience_activation in experimental_features. Per docs/reference/experimental-status, it MAY change between 3.x releases with notice.

oneOf.title: AdCP audience sync
oneOf.description: The seller accepts inline audience member pushes via the AdCP sync_audiences task. Any AdCP-speaking buyer can use this path with no additional integration. This pattern declares inline push only; grant- and distribution-based paths carry their own declarations.

oneOf.title: TMP identity match
oneOf.description: The seller has configured Trusted Match Protocol identity-match calls to a specific buyer agent. Declarations are per buyer agent because the integration is not generic. Entries MUST be consistent with trusted_match.providers[] where both are present on the product.

agent_url.description: Buyer agent's registered agent URL. Canonical identifier, mirroring trusted_match.providers[].agent_url.

oneOf.title: File transfer
oneOf.description: Bucket-addressed file exchange over a cloud storage protocol. The buyer moves the bytes; direction declares who hosts the bucket.

directions.description: Supported transfer directions. buyer_to_seller: buyer writes to a seller-hosted bucket. seller_to_buyer: seller reads from a buyer-hosted bucket. Absent means unspecified (resolve during account setup), not neither.

vendor.description: Platform providing the storage primitive (e.g., the cloud provider's domain).

oneOf.title: Dataset query
oneOf.description: Vendor-mediated query access: the seller reads a dataset the buyer shares through the vendor's grantee-identified sharing mechanism (e.g., Snowflake Secure Data Sharing, Databricks Delta Sharing, BigQuery authorized views). Admissible only when the grant names a principal and no secret is conveyed; token-bearer flows remain out-of-band.

vendor.description: Data-sharing platform the seller can consume from.

consumer_identities.description: Principals the buyer grants access to in the vendor's system. identity is always required. cloud and region are optional, paired deployment metadata: omit both for global principals (for example, an IAM principal or federated identity). Their operational meaning is vendor-specific — they may constrain direct-share reachability or select a fulfillment route, or may be routing and cost hints only. They are not compliance boundaries; data-transfer assessments key on the recipient entity's jurisdiction, not the grantee account's region. Optional: sellers MAY instead communicate identities during account setup.

cloud.description: Cloud family hosting this identity's account.

region.description: Vendor/cloud region identifier. Format follows the cloud family's region naming; not constrained by this schema.

identity.description: Principal to grant, interpreted relative to the enclosing entry's vendor.domain. Format is vendor-specific and opaque — Snowflake: orgname.accountname; Databricks: sharing recipient identifier; BigQuery: IAM principal.

oneOf.title: Clean room
oneOf.description: Privacy-preserving match in the named vendor's clean room; neither party sees the other's raw rows. A seller MUST declare this audience-activation pattern only when the collaboration can produce an audience targetable on this product; analytics-only or measurement-only room access does not qualify. The declaration does not imply that output is portable. Room setup is bilateral onboarding. Platform-native or partner-distributed output pairs with platform_distribution; queryable output pairs with dataset_query. The resulting audience binds through a dataset or platform_segment source reference on sync_audiences (core/audience-source.json).

oneOf.title: Platform distribution
oneOf.description: The vendor's rails deliver segments to the seller's destination; the buyer initiates distribution in the vendor's system and binds the arriving segment with a platform_segment source reference on sync_audiences (core/audience-source.json). destination_ref is optional because many vendors create or reveal the account-scoped destination only during bilateral account setup.

destination_ref.description: Opaque, account-scoped destination or seat reference in the vendor's system, as the buyer needs it to initiate distribution. A seller-declared configuration reference, not a buyer-invoked key or secret. Sellers MUST NOT publish one global reference when the vendor configuration is buyer- or account-specific. Omit until account setup has established the destination.

bind_expiry_days.description: Window after which the seller MAY expire an unfulfilled platform_segment bind (per-audience action: failed on sync_audiences). Initial vendor distribution is days-scale; windows shorter than the vendor's documented distribution latency are non-conformant.

external:enums/representation-selection-.title: Representation Selection Strategy
external:enums/representation-selection-.description: Deterministic strategy used after filtering a CreativeRepresentationSet against one seller destination contract. `representation_order` selects the first compatible representation in source array order. `highest_compatible_vast` is valid only when the destination format_kind is `video_vast` or `audio_vast`; it selects the compatible VAST representation with the highest exact VAST version, and equal-version ties are resolved by source array order. Using it for another format is INVALID_REQUEST and never falls back silently.

external:enums/creative-selection-strate.title: Creative Selection Strategy
external:enums/creative-selection-strate.description: How a creative agent samples which catalog items / signal conditions to produce creatives for when max_creatives is below the eligible count (#5262). Selection ordering surfaces on the existing rank/recommended fields of build_creative's creatives[].variants[]. This is a curated set, not an open extension point — new strategies are added per the enum-membership criterion in spec-guidelines.md. Part of the experimental signal-fanout surface (x-status: experimental; feature id `creative.signal_fanout`).

enumDescriptions.audience_relevance: Rank by relevance to the buyer's audience signal(s) — the user-side axis. Drawn from the SAME signal_ref pointers in signal_conditions / package targeting, not a parallel signals[] array.
enumDescriptions.contextual_fit: Rank by fit to the content/context the creative renders against — the content-side counterpart to audience_relevance (user-side). Uses the same signal_ref mechanism with a context signal rather than an audience signal. Mirrors the Trusted Match Protocol Context Match / Identity Match split.
enumDescriptions.performance: Rank by the catalog item's historical delivery performance (e.g. CTR, completion, conversion) where the agent has that signal.
enumDescriptions.proximity: Rank by proximity to a location input. Reuse the existing geo targeting shape (see docs/media-buy/advanced-topics/targeting.mdx) rather than a parallel one; the exact geo-input binding is still being settled, which the experimental status of this surface keeps revisable.
enumDescriptions.inventory_priority: Rank by seller-side catalog metadata (margin, overstock, promotional priority). No buyer input.
enumDescriptions.random: Status-quo fallback: agent samples without a ranking preference. Default when selection_strategy is omitted.

external:core/creative-operation-format-.title: Creative Operation Format Declaration
external:core/creative-operation-format-.description: Authority-free canonical format declaration used by creative.supported_formats[]. It describes what a creative agent can build, validate, or preview. It preserves canonical parameter validation and creative-route macro processing capabilities, but MUST NOT carry seller production authority such as tracker_execution_contract or tracker_execution_contract_digest.

format_option_id.description: Stable publisher- or product-declaration identity that this creative operation can satisfy. When publisher_domain is present, this field is required.

publisher_domain.description: Publisher namespace for format_option_id when this operation claims compatibility with a publisher declaration.

macro_resolution_capabilities.description: Creative-route processing capabilities for exact macro dialect identities, semantics, operations, actors, contexts, and encodings. These capabilities describe build, validation, or preview processing and do not grant seller production authority.

verifier_constraints.translation_chain_closure: every translate_to_native entry must have an exact matching resolve_value entry for its translation_target in this same array

params.description: Canonical creative-shape parameters. Validate against the schema selected by format_kind; custom params validate against the fetched format_schema.

allOf.$comment: Creative operation declarations never carry seller production authority. The explicit prohibition remains effective even though the object is open for forward-compatible creative metadata.

canonical_params.custom: validate params against fetched format_schema uri and digest

external:core/creative-locale-policy.jso.title: Creative Locale Policy
external:core/creative-locale-policy.jso.description: Seller-declared locale eligibility for one product or placement format declaration. Each accepted_language_ranges entry is a concrete canonical BCP 47 language range evaluated with RFC 4647 section 3.3.1 Basic Filtering: fr accepts fr, fr-CA, and fr-FR, while fr-CA accepts only fr-CA and its more-specific descendants. Ranges are ORed and wildcards are not supported. Presence is a hard assignment constraint, not a preference: at least one materialized creative locale variant must match. The seller filters the creative to eligible variants before applying buyer-declared strict Lookup, locale_fallbacks, or default behavior; buyer policy can never select a seller-ineligible variant.

accepted_language_ranges.description: Concrete canonical BCP 47 language ranges accepted by this format option. RFC 4647 Basic Filtering is directional: seller range fr accepts variant fr-CA, but seller range fr-CA does not accept variant fr or fr-FR. Use zxx explicitly for language-neutral creative; und means unknown and is not a wildcard.

external:core/format-id.json.title: Format Reference (Structured Object)
external:core/format-id.json.description: **DEPRECATED in 3.2.** Legacy named-format reference retained for 3.x compatibility. This JSON object — never a plain string — identifies a format by its declaring agent and local slug, and may carry legacy logical dimensions, pixel ratio, or duration parameters. New products and manifests use canonical `format_options`, `format_kind`, and `format_option_ref`; creative-agent build routing uses `creative.supported_formats[].capability_id`.

agent_url.description: URL of the agent that defines this format (e.g., 'https://creative.adcontextprotocol.org' for standard formats, or 'https://publisher.com/.well-known/adcp/sales' for custom formats). Callers comparing two `format-id` values MUST canonicalize `agent_url` per the AdCP URL canonicalization rules before treating two formats as the same. See docs/reference/url-canonicalization.

id.description: Format identifier within the agent's namespace (e.g., 'display_static', 'video_hosted', 'audio_standard'). When used alone, references a template format. When combined with dimension/duration fields, creates a parameterized format ID for a specific variant.

width.description: Width in pixels for visual formats. When specified, height must also be specified. Both fields together create a parameterized format ID for dimension-specific variants.

height.description: Height in pixels for visual formats. When specified, width must also be specified. Both fields together create a parameterized format ID for dimension-specific variants.

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds for time-based formats (video, audio). When specified, creates a parameterized format ID. Omit to reference a template format without parameters.

pixel_ratio.description: Required intrinsic-pixel density for a parameterized visual format, expressed as intrinsic pixels per logical pixel. Requires `width` and `height`. Example: `{id: "display_image", width: 300, height: 250, pixel_ratio: 2}` identifies a 300×250 logical render supplied by a 600×500 image. Omit for the backward-compatible 1x variant.

external:core/platform-extension-ref.jso.title: Platform Extension Reference
external:core/platform-extension-ref.jso.description:
Reference to a platform extension definition. The agent that owns the URI is authoritative for the extension's schema. Buyers fetch the definition once per content digest and cache it. Platform extensions are typically bundled in `get_products` responses under an `extensions` map keyed by `uri@digest`, eliminating the need for a separate fetch.

**Within a single response**, multiple references to the same `uri` MUST carry the same `digest` — divergent digests in one response indicate producer-side error (e.g., concurrent extension revision mid-render). Buyers encountering divergent digests for the same URI MUST fail closed: treat all references to that URI as unresolved and surface a validation error rather than picking one branch silently. **Across responses**, digest divergence is normal — extension authors revise their schemas, the new digest differs, the cache key changes, and the buyer refetches. Cache by `uri@digest`, not by `uri` alone.

uri.description: HTTPS URL identifying the extension. `https://` is mandatory — `http://`, `file://`, `data:`, and other schemes are rejected at the schema layer (defense-in-depth on top of the fetch-contract normative rules). The URI base is the owning agent's URL; the path identifies the extension within that agent. Example: 'https://creative.adcontextprotocol.org/translated/meta/extensions/meta_pixel'. The full fetch contract — SSRF allowlist, response-size cap, $ref sandbox, schema-compile bounds — is documented on `product-format-declaration.json#format_schema` and applies to ALL fetches of this reference shape regardless of whether the field is named `format_schema` (load-bearing for validation) or `platform_extensions` (informational); the *transport* rules are identical, only the *consumption* semantics differ.

digest.description: SHA-256 content digest of the extension definition (sha256:<hex>). Used to detect drift — if the agent revises the extension, the digest changes and cached definitions become invalid.

external:core/canonical-format-kind.json.title: Canonical Format Kind
external:core/canonical-format-kind.json.description: Discriminator naming one of the 15 AdCP 3.2 canonical creative formats, plus `custom` for adopter-defined shapes. AdCP 3.2 adds `audio_vast` for VAST-tag-delivered audio (the standards-conformant profile starts at VAST 4.1, with older versions available only as seller-declared legacy interoperability) and promotes the legacy `multi_state_display` and `multi_placement_takeover` custom shapes to `seller_rendered_stateful_display` and `coordinated_placements`. When `format_kind` is `custom`, the declaration also carries `format_shape` and `format_schema`. The enum mirrors the branches in `product-format-declaration.json` and is closed for producer validation: sellers do not mint ad-hoc values. SDKs may retain unknown future values in tolerant in-memory parsers, but that does not change versioned JSON Schema validation. A seller responding to a 3.1-or-earlier request MUST project away 3.2-only kinds and emit a compatible legacy declaration; a strict older schema correctly rejects an unprojected newer kind. See adcp#3666 and the promotion migration contract in canonical-formats.mdx.

external:core/vendor-metric-id.json.title: Vendor Metric ID
external:core/vendor-metric-id.json.description: Identifier for a vendor-defined metric within the vendor's vocabulary. Stable lookup key; the vendor publishes the canonical list (with category, methodology, and standard alignment) in `brand.json` `agents[type='measurement']`. Lowercase with underscores so a future enum promotion into `available-metric.json` is a literal string lift. Identifier is namespaced by the vendor — the same `metric_id` may mean different things in different vendors' vocabularies.

external:enums/specialism.json.title: AdCP Specialism

An agent asserts specialisms it supports in get_adcp_capabilities; the AAO compliance runner executes the matching storyboards to verify the claim.

Promotes to `stable` when the SI tools graduate from `x-status: experimental`. See https://github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp/issues/3961.
